I’m now resolving the exact sampled policies, trajectories, diagnostics, and keyframes—including the assigned parent’s inherited log—before deciding the gate and signs.

The signed fore–aft gate is worse still. I’m tracing the normalized observation conventions and the exact closest-approach sequence now so the next candidate changes one genuinely distinct mechanism rather than retuning this closed branch.

The visual-evidence workflow changed the policy direction materially: the candidate will not tune either failed distance gate. It will preserve the best controller exactly until the target actually crosses behind the fish, then correct the bearing sign one-sidedly—the first state event that occurs after, rather than before, the best sampled close pass.

The single candidate and both required records are now updated. The durable lesson explicitly closes the two radial-recovery windows and the symmetric fore–aft attenuation branch, while keeping one-sided longitudinal overshoot as a falsifiable next mechanism.
